page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-96 is a compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 192 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. It has a large L3 cache of 260 MB, alongside 2 MB of L2 cache and 48 KB of L1d cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-highcpu-96 demonstrates strong multi-core performance, achieving a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21998.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 82913.7. The processor's advanced instruction support, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_tile and AMX_int8), contributes to strong performance in specialized workloads. This is reflected in a top-tier Passmark CPU encryption test score of 86639.74 and strong LLM inference prompt processing speeds, reaching 294.08 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. Memory bandwidth is also robust, with read-only cached small block bandwidth measured at 6406.28 GB/sec and large block write bandwidth at 127.91 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highcpu-96 offers high compute density and specialized instruction sets without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. This makes it highly efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include high-throughput web serving, software compilation, cryptography, data compression, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
